My research connects nanoscale process development and heterogeneous materials integration with single-molecule measurement. I study how fabrication, pore geometry, material interfaces, and molecular structure influence transport and ionic-current signals in solid-state and hybrid nanopores.

## Research projects

### DNA origami hybrid nanopores

Programmable DNA nanostructures modify the sensing environment of a solid-state nanopore. Our published work examined confinement, DNA–protein interactions, and enhanced sensitivity for holo-human serum transferrin. [Project details](projects/dna-origami.qmd).

### Multilayer heterostructure nanopores

I applied the laboratory’s existing CT-CDB method to silicon nitride structures incorporating graphene, MoS₂, and hBN, studying material interfaces, electric fields, and directional protein transport. [Project details](projects/heterostructures.qmd).

### DNA-hosted silver nanoclusters

This published study examines voltage-dependent translocation and electrolyte-dependent stability of DNA-hosted silver nanoclusters, comparing DNA templates with and without clusters. [Project details](projects/silver-nanoclusters.qmd).

### α-Hemolysin hybrid nanopores

My ongoing work investigates α-hemolysin integration with glass nanopipettes through electrophoretic capture. The research examines device stability, electrical characteristics, experimental troubleshooting, and signal analysis.

### Programmable nanopore fabrication

I contributed to P.O.R.E., a low-cost programmable fabrication platform, including electrical control, instrumentation integration, platform characterization, and experimental validation. [Project details](projects/instrumentation.qmd).

### Multiphysics modeling and machine learning

Electric-field simulations and event-level signal analysis help relate device architecture to transport behavior and support classification of experimental signals. [Project details](projects/modeling-ml.qmd).

## Research methods

Solid-state and hybrid nanopore fabrication; CT-CDB; heterogeneous membrane integration; ionic-current acquisition; electrical, SEM, and AFM characterization; experimental signal analysis; COMSOL modeling; statistical analysis and machine learning.
